quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
rationale: Section 20 meets and exceeds the preferred position. 20.1 gives a Vendor defend/indemnify/hold-harmless obligation covering Customer and its Affiliates for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims relating to the Services or Deliverables, with no customer-modification/combination/specification carve-outs. 20.2 adds the remaining preferred triggers: Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud (plus bodily injury/property damage). 20.4 supplies standard procedure (prompt notice with a material-prejudice qualifier, cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, control of defence, and no adverse settlement without consent). 20.5 provides the infringement remedies (procure, modify/replace, or terminate and refund) expressly "in addition to" the defence obligation, and bars Vendor from terminating unaffected Services. The Customer-side indemnity in 20.3 is appropriately narrow — limited to unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized and Customer's violation of Applicable Law — with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modification, combination or instructions. Direction is correct: the substantive burden falls on Vendor. Liability treatment also favours us: Section 21.3 defines "Excluded Claims" to include a Party's indemnification obligations, IP infringement, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud, so Vendor's indemnity sits outside the 21.1 cap entirely — better than the fallback's 3x super-cap. Section 19.4 and 19.5 further confirm no warranty remedy or disclaimer limits the indemnities. No redline required.

Customer's reciprocal indemnity in 20.3 is appropriately narrow (unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized; Customer's violation of Applicable Law) with Vendor Technology/modification/combination/instruction carve-outs, so direction of burden is correct. 21.3 places indemnification obligations, IP infringement and gross negligence/wilful misconduct within Excluded Claims, so Vendor's indemnity is uncapped — better than the fallback super-cap; the rationale's reliance on this is accurate. quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
rationale: Section 21 meets the preferred position in full. (1) Cap: § 21.1 is expressly mutual ("each Party's total aggregate liability"; "The cap is mutual") and set at the greater of Fees "paid or payable" by Customer in the twelve months preceding the event and USD 1,000,000 — the exact basis and floor we require, using the preferred "paid or payable" formulation rather than "paid". (2) Cap base is not illusory: "Fees" (§ 1.5, p0007) means recurring subscription, professional services, usage and other Order Form amounts, i.e. substantive recurring revenue; the carve-out of a one-time implementation charge does not undermine the base, and the USD 1,000,000 floor protects against a low-fee first year. (3) Indirect damages: § 21.2 excludes consequential/indirect damages mutually ("neither Party"), and helpfully deems data-restoration, replacement services, breach notification and incident response costs to be direct damages — better than our position. (4) Carve-outs: "Excluded Claims" (§ 21.3) sits outside both the cap and the consequential-damages exclusion and covers every required item — breach of confidentiality, data-protection or security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement/misappropriation of the other Party's IP. So the § 20.1 IP indemnity, § 20.2 data-breach indemnity, and §§ 15–17 data/confidentiality/security obligations are all uncapped. (5) § 21.3 also confirms Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is not "damages" and is not limited by the section, as we require. No competing or one-sided cap is hidden elsewhere: searches for "liability" and "exceed" return only § 18 insurance limits and § 22 audit-cost language, and §§ 19–20 contain no aggregate-liability or sole-remedy cap (§ 20.5 adds a refund remedy "in addition to" Vendor's defence obligations). § 21.4 is standard savings language. No redline required.

ops.newText: For ninety (90) days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria, provided that for any Deliverable that consists of or embeds software or Vendor Technology licensed to Customer on a paid-up or perpetual basis, that period is twelve (12) months.

quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.
rationale:
On re-examination there is a genuine parametric shortfall, not merely the formatting false negative I reported twice before. The preferred position requires twelve months of conformity for SOFTWARE and ninety days for services. The document's definitions split software into two tracks and only one is adequately warranted:

(1) Section 1.7 defines "Services" as the HOSTED software plus implementation and related services. Hosted software is fully covered: Section 19.2 warrants Hosted Services conformity "throughout the subscription term", which meets or exceeds the twelve-month software benchmark.

(2) Section 13.2, however, expressly contemplates "software and Vendor Technology delivered to Customer on a paid-up basis or embedded in a Deliverable", granting us a perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid licence. That software is not hosted, so the full-term Hosted Services warranty does not reach it. Section 1.4 defines "Deliverable" as reports, configurations, integrations, specifications, designs, workflows and training materials and expressly EXCLUDES Vendor Technology. So perpetually licensed software reaches the conformity warranty only when embedded in a Deliverable, and then only for ninety days — the fallback level, not the preferred twelve months. Standalone paid-up Vendor Technology arguably carries no durational conformity period at all.

REDLINE: a single minimal amendment to Section 19.2 extends the period to twelve (12) months for any Deliverable that consists of or embeds software or Vendor Technology licensed on a paid-up or perpetual basis, leaving ninety days for all other (services-type) Deliverables. This also renders the period in numerals, which resolves the deterministic period check that failed on the spelled-out "ninety days". Fallback: ninety days across the board if Vendor confirms software is always delivered hosted.

ALL OTHER ELEMENTS REMAIN COMPLIANT and are untouched: 19.1 professional/workmanlike plus material conformity; 19.3 malicious code and Applicable Law; 19.4 re-perform/repair/replace with termination-and-refund backstop, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims; 19.5 disclaims implied warranties only and preserves express warranties, so no carve-out edit is needed. The ninety-day clock also runs from the later of delivery or acceptance, which is better than the delivery-only benchmark. Separately noted: the 19.3 malicious-code warranty covers only code "intentionally introduced by Vendor", narrower than a flat no-malicious-code warranty; left unflagged as standard market language given the non-exclusive remedy and security obligations carried as Excluded Claims under 21.3.
